en.name: Almond oil
en.summary: Almond oil keeps 1 year from purchase in the pantry, or 2 years refrigerated at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. Like every nut oil it fails by going rancid rather than by growing anything, and the drivers are light, heat, air and time.
en.pantry: 1 year from purchase in a cool, dark cupboard with the cap on tight. Almond oil is a nut oil, usually cold-pressed and often unrefined, which means it still carries the minor compounds that give it flavour — and those are exactly what oxidises. Rancidity is not a pathogen question: it is a slow chemical reaction with oxygen, sped up by light, by heat and by the air in a half-empty bottle. This is why a dark glass bottle kept away from the hob matters far more than the printed date, and why the cupboard next to the stove is the worst place in the kitchen for any oil.
en.fridge: 2 years from purchase at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, which is double what the cupboard gives — a big enough difference that it is worth the shelf space for a bottle you use slowly. Cold almond oil may go cloudy or thick; that is the oil partly solidifying and is completely harmless, and it clears again at room temperature. Decant a small working amount into a separate bottle for the counter and keep the main bottle cold.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is published for almond oil, and freezing is not useful. Oil does not freeze into a solid the way water does, so you gain nothing in convenience, and the refrigerator already gives the full doubling of shelf life. The one real benefit of very cold storage — slowing oxidation — is already captured at fridge temperature.
en.thawing: Let a cold bottle stand at room temperature until it is clear and pourable again. Do not warm it over the hob or in hot water: heat is one of the things that ages an oil.
spoilage: A sharp, crayon-like or paint smell — rancid oil, and the decisive sign.
A bitter, scratchy finish at the back of the throat.
Colour darkened noticeably from its original pale gold.
Any sediment in a refined oil, or a musty smell from a bottle stored warm.
tips: Buy small bottles; the clock runs faster once air fills the headspace.
Keep it away from the hob — heat ages oil faster than time does.
Dark glass or a tin beats a clear bottle every time.
Smell it before you use it in anything uncooked; rancidity is unmistakable.

faq.q: How long does almond oil last?
faq.a: 1 year from purchase in a cool dark cupboard, or 2 years refrigerated at 4 °C (40 °F) or below.
It doubles the shelf life, so yes for a bottle you use slowly. It may go cloudy or thick in the cold, which is harmless and clears at room temperature.

faq.q: How can you tell if almond oil has gone rancid?
faq.a: Smell it. A sharp, crayon or paint-like note is decisive, and rancid oil tastes bitter and scratchy at the back of the throat.

zh.name: 杏仁油
zh.summary: 杏仁油自購買日起放櫃子可放 1 年，放 4 °C 以下冷藏則是 2 年。和所有堅果油一樣，它的失敗方式是油耗而不是長東西，而推動它的是光、熱、空氣和時間。
zh.pantry: 自購買日起 1 年，放陰涼避光的櫃子，瓶蓋鎖緊。杏仁油是堅果油，通常冷壓、而且往往未精煉，也就是說那些帶來風味的微量成分都還在——而那些正是會氧化的東西。油耗不是病原菌的問題：它是一個和氧氣進行的緩慢化學反應，被光、熱以及半空瓶子裡的空氣加速。所以「深色玻璃瓶、遠離爐火」這件事，遠比瓶身上的日期重要；而爐台旁邊那個櫃子，是全廚房對任何油來說最糟的位置。
zh.fridge: 自購買日起放 4 °C 以下 2 年，是櫃子的兩倍——差距大到值得為一瓶用得慢的油空出位置。冰過的杏仁油可能變濁、變稠，那是油脂部分凝固，完全無害，回到室溫就會恢復清澈。可以另外分裝一小瓶放檯面日常使用，主瓶留在冷藏。
zh.freezer: 杏仁油沒有公布的冷凍期限，冷凍也沒有用。油不像水那樣會凍成硬塊，所以使用上沒有任何方便可言；而且冷藏已經給了你完整的兩倍壽命。低溫唯一真正的好處——拖慢氧化——在冷藏溫度就已經拿到了。
zh.thawing: 把冰過的瓶子放在室溫，等它恢復清澈、倒得動即可。不要拿去爐火上或泡熱水加溫：熱正是讓油老化的原因之一。
spoilage: 聞起來刺鼻、像蠟筆或油漆味——那就是油耗，而且是決定性的。
入口後喉頭有苦味和刮喉感。
顏色比原本的淡金色明顯變深。
精煉油出現沉澱，或放在溫暖處的瓶子聞起來有霉味。
tips: 買小瓶；瓶子一空一半、空氣進去，計時就走得更快。
遠離爐火——熱讓油老化的速度比時間還快。
深色玻璃瓶或鐵罐永遠勝過透明瓶。
要用在不加熱的料理前先聞一下；油耗味非常好認。

faq.a: 自購買日起放陰涼避光處 1 年，或 4 °C 以下冷藏 2 年。
冷藏可以把壽命翻一倍，所以用得慢的那瓶值得冰。冰了可能變濁變稠，那是無害的，回到室溫就清了。

faq.q: 怎麼知道杏仁油油耗了？
faq.a: 聞一下。刺鼻、像蠟筆或油漆的味道就是決定性的；油耗的油吃起來會苦、還會刮喉嚨。
